name: Grab
summary: Grab's careers site says its process runs up to four rounds tailored to the role, takes about a month on average, and that each interview usually lasts 30 minutes to an hour. For engineers it describes a recruiter or HR call, live coding on data structures and algorithms, a system design discussion where you justify your decisions, and a conversation about Grab's values, the 4Hs: Heart, Hunger, Honour and Humility. Analyst and business roles commonly report a case study instead of coding.
rounds: Recruiter or HR call about your background and past work
Live coding: one or two problems on an online platform (engineering)
System design: a whiteboarding discussion on scalable systems, security and monitoring (experienced engineers)
Culture and hiring manager conversation about Grab's 4Hs
Offer, often about a month after the first call
looks_for: Heart: caring for customers, partners and each other
Problem-solving with data structures and algorithms

questions.text: Tell me about a time you went out of your way for a customer or partner.
covers: Who they were and what they needed
What you did beyond the usual
The result for them

questions.text: Tell me about a time you were wrong and how you handled it.
covers: What you got wrong
How you owned it and fixed it
What you do differently now

questions.text: Tell me about a goal you set yourself that was hard to reach.
covers: The goal and why it mattered
Obstacles and how you pushed through
The result

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to choose between doing something fast and doing it right.
covers: The pressure and the risk
How you decided
What happened and what you learned

questions.text: How would you design the system that matches a ride request to a nearby driver?
covers: Driver locations, spatial indexing and how often they update
Matching logic and handling no driver nearby
Scaling for peak hours and monitoring

questions.text: How would you design food delivery time estimates that customers can trust?
covers: Signals: restaurant prep time, distance, traffic, rider availability
Updating the estimate as things change
Measuring accuracy and fixing bias

questions.text: Given a list of trips with start and end times, how would you find the maximum number happening at once?
covers: Sorting start and end events
A sweep with a running count
Time and space complexity, and edge cases

questions.text: How would you keep a payments wallet secure from account takeover?
covers: Device checks, step-up verification and limits
Spotting unusual behaviour
Recovery that doesn't lock out real users

questions.text: A city's ride cancellations jumped this week. How would you find out why?
covers: Splitting by rider, driver, area and time
Checking for releases, weather or events
A hypothesis, a test and a fix

questions.text: How would you adapt a product for markets with different payment habits and phone types?
covers: Local payment methods, including cash
Low-end phones and patchy networks
How you'd learn from each market

questions.text: Why do you want to work at Grab?
covers: Something specific about Grab's mission in Southeast Asia
How your skills fit the team
The impact you'd like to have

questions.text: Which of Grab's 4Hs comes most naturally to you, and which do you work on?
covers: An honest pick for each
An example of each
What you're doing to grow

tips: Prepare a story for each of the 4Hs: Heart, Hunger, Honour and Humility.
In system design, say why you made each decision; Grab describes the round as a discussion where you justify your choices.
Practise coding on an online editor without autocomplete, talking through your approach.
Think about Southeast Asian users: cash payments, low-end phones, many languages and patchy networks.

sources.title: Grab Careers: How we hire engineers
